title: GDD T-101 — InputInterpreter: tap/hold/mash derivation, debounce, diagonal collapse (§3.2/§3.3)
description: Engine-free input-interpretation layer in Barcade.Core per Barcade_GDD_Tecnico.md §3 (repo root; read §3.1–3.3 and Annex D.1 before coding). Consumes the existing InputSnapshot stream (60 Hz fixed ticks) and derives, per seat, the signals the GDD says are computed by an InputInterpreter and NOT stored in PlayerInput: press/release edges, tap (release within 150 ms of press), hold duration in ticks, and mash frequency over a 500 ms sliding window with the §3.3 response curve (below 2 Hz counts as 0, saturation at 9 Hz, fuerza = clamp01((f-2)/7)). Includes tick-level debounce so contact bounce never mints extra edges, a diagonal-collapse helper (diagonals collapse to the most-recent dominant cardinal, §3.2 anti-ghosting) for 4-direction consumers like IGUALA, and a Reset() that discards hold/mash accumulation when entering MG_INTRO (no input bleed between microgames). Curve/window parameters are constructor-injected (GameTuning-ready), never hardcoded. This is the root dependency of Hito 1 (GDD tasks T-102/T-103/T-104 build on it). Reuse existing Core conventions in Barcade/Assets/Barcade/Core/Runtime (C#9, no UnityEngine, no System.Random); fast tests mirror Core in fast-tests/Barcade.Core.FastTests.
acceptance_criteria: An engine-free InputInterpreter in Barcade.Core consumes successive InputSnapshot ticks and exposes per-seat derived signals: ButtonPressedThisTick, ButtonReleasedThisTick, HoldDurationTicks, and MashFrequencyHz (sliding 500 ms window)

Tap is a rising edge whose release follows within <= 150 ms (9 ticks at 60 Hz); hold is rising edge + accumulated duration; the three button modes are distinguishable by a consumer that uses exactly one mode (GDD exclusion rule)
Mash response curve per GDD 3.3: below minHz (2) yields 0, linear up to satHz (9), fuerza = clamp01((f-minHz)/(satHz-minHz)); minHz/satHz/window are constructor parameters, not constants
Debounce: a spurious single-tick flip-back (bounce within the 8 ms hardware window, i.e. sub-tick glitch modeled at tick granularity) does not produce extra press/release edges or extra mash counts
Diagonal collapse helper: Direction8 diagonals collapse to the most-recent dominant cardinal component, stable across the 1-2 tick N->NE->E transit described in GDD 3.2
Reset() clears accumulated hold/mash/edge state so no input state leaks across microgame boundaries
Steady-state Tick performs zero heap allocations and the interpreter is deterministic given the same snapshot sequence (replay-safe)

Tests-first: failing fast-suite tests encoding each rule above are committed (test: commit) strictly before any implementation commit, with the red run captured as evidence; full fast suite green afterwards (baseline 323 tests must not regress)

comments.body: Implemented tests-first on master, no push (by dev-t101). Commits: 1e5e94f test(core) failing InputInterpreter spec (30 tests; red evidence = CS0246 compile errors against the not-yet-existing types, the expected TDD-red for brand-new types) STRICTLY BEFORE e20d6f8 feat(core) InputInterpreter. Fast suite 323 -> 353, all green, 0 skipped. New Core files under Barcade/Assets/Barcade/Core/Runtime/Input/: Direction8.cs, InputInterpreterConfig.cs (ctor-injected ticksPerSecond/tapWindowTicks/mashMinHz/mashSatHz/mashWindowSeconds; GddDefaults = 60/9/2/9/0.5), InputInterpreter.cs (per-seat edges/tap/hold/mash + MashForce clamp01((hz-min)/(sat-min)), RawDirection, CollapsedCardinal, static ToDirection8 + CollapseDiagonal; Tick(IReadOnlyPlayerInputs); Reset() clears seat state not tick clock). Tests in Assets/Tests/EditMode/InputInterpreterTests.cs incl. zero-alloc proof (GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread over 1000 ticks after warmup) and tick-by-tick determinism test. Design notes: 2-consecutive-tick confirm debounce (uniform 1-tick edge latency); diagonal cold-start resolves to horizontal component (mirrors InputSnapshot.CardinalDirection tie-break); stick-to-None does NOT clear dominant-cardinal memory, only Reset() does; 64-slot press-timestamp ring buffer per seat. FLAGGED DELTA vs GDD listing: existing Core InputSnapshot is per-seat (no session wrapper/Tick field), stores continuous StickX/StickY (Direction8 newly added), and upstream ButtonState.Pressed already bakes un-debounced edge detection — interpreter treats Pressed||Held as raw down and re-derives edges itself; legacy consumers (e.g. AporreaMicrogame) still receive un-debounced Pressed — follow-up ticket candidate.
